newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's July CPI +1.0 vs +1.1 pct in June.
newsitem.headline: Israel's July CPI +1.0 vs +1.1 pct in June.

text.p: The Central Bureau of Statistics issued the following economic indicator on Friday:
ISRAEL CONSUMER PRICES Jul 97 Jun 97 Jul 96
Note: To compare previous indices based on 1987=100.0, multiply indices from January 1994 by 2.421.

The Central Bureau of Statistics said the index was boosted by higher prices of food, health, education, culture and entertainment but the biggest contributor was housing prices which rose 2.5 percent for the month, largely influenced by the devaluation of the shekel against dollar in June. Israeli housing prices are generally denominated in dollars. The overall index without housing would have risen 0.5 percent in July.
The wholesale price index rose 0.9 percent in July. Consumer prices have risen 6.0 percent since the start of the year.

The CPI was at the low end of economists' expectations. Economists had said a high CPI would prompt Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel to raise interest rates at the end of the month. He slashed the base rate by 1.2 percentage points to 12.7 percent in mid-June and has held them at that level since, despite a high June CPI.
Economists said they expected Frenkel to raise rates by 0.3 to 0.5 percentage points. There was no immediate reaction from the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, which does not trade on Fridays.
